desc:
Deleting the character at position i of s costs cost[i]. Delete some characters (possibly none) so that the string that remains is exactly t, and return the minimum total cost of the deletions. If this is impossible, return -1.

s = "abcab", cost = [4,1,3,2,5], t = "ab"  ->  6   (keep positions 0 and 4, delete 1, 2, 3)
s = "xy",    cost = [1,1],         t = "yx"  -> -1
s = "aa",    cost = [5,2],         t = "a"   ->  2   (keep the expensive one)
s = "abc",   cost = [1,1,1],       t = ""    ->  3
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
hints: Total deletion cost = (sum of all costs) - (sum of the costs of the characters you keep). So maximise what you keep.
The kept characters must spell t, in order, as a subsequence of s. Different ways to choose that subsequence keep different total costs.

Let best[j] be the maximum kept cost for matching the first j characters of t using the characters of s seen so far. Process s left to right and update j from high to low: best[j] = max(best[j], best[j-1] + cost[i]) when s[i] == t[j-1].
editorial: The deletion cost equals sum(cost) - kept, where kept is the total cost of the surviving characters. The survivors form a subsequence of s equal to t, so the task becomes: among all occurrences of t as a subsequence of s, find the one with maximum total weight. A plain greedy match picks the earliest positions, which is not necessarily the heaviest.

Use a one-dimensional table: best[j] is the maximum weight with which the first j characters of t can be matched using the prefix of s processed so far, or minus infinity if impossible, with best[0] = 0. For each character of s, scan j downwards so every character of s is used at most once, and apply best[j] = max(best[j], best[j-1] + cost[i]) whenever the letters agree. The answer is sum(cost) - best[len(t)], or -1 if best[len(t)] is still minus infinity. The running time is O(len(s) · len(t)).
